title: Shallow Clone with Property Descriptors
subtopicTitle: Object Descriptors & Deep Cloning with Circular References
problemStatement: Implement `shallowCloneWithDescriptors(obj)` that copies all own properties (enumerable and non-enumerable, including getters/setters and Symbols) using `Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptors` and `Object.create`.
interviewTrap: Using `{ ...obj }` or `Object.assign` turns getter properties into plain value properties evaluated during copy, destroying the dynamic getter.

testCases.name: Preserves dynamic getter behavior
testCases.testFn: const orig = { text: 'hello', get upper() { return this.text.toUpperCase(); } }; const clone = shallowCloneWithDescriptors(orig); orig.text = 'world'; return clone.upper;

testCases.name: Preserves non-enumerable properties
testCases.testFn: const orig = {}; Object.defineProperty(orig, 'secret', { value: 123, enumerable: false }); const clone = shallowCloneWithDescriptors(orig); return clone.secret;

testCases.name: Retains prototype of original object
testCases.testFn: class Sample {} const orig = new Sample(); const clone = shallowCloneWithDescriptors(orig); return clone instanceof Sample;

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(obj))` drops undefined, functions, Symbols, Date (turned to string), RegExp, and throws TypeError on circular references. Production deep clones require a WeakMap visited tracker.
stepByStepWalkthrough: 1. Initialize execution context and environment records for Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptors & Property Integrity.
2. Execute logic adhering to ECMAScript standard specification.
3. Verify invariant boundaries and edge conditions.
detailedExplanation.underlyingEngineInternals: In JavaScript engines (e.g. V8), Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptors & Property Integrity is optimized via inline caches, heap contexts, and bytecode translation.
edgeCasesHandled: Using `{ ...obj }` or `Object.assign` turns getter properties into plain value properties evaluated during copy, destroying the dynamic getter.

verifiedRules: Adheres to ECMAScript runtime evaluation specifications.

interviewCrossQuestions.question: Why does Object.assign or spread {...obj} fail to preserve property descriptors?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: `Object.assign` and spread use standard `[[Get]]` and `[[Set]]` operations. They read only enumerable own properties and assign them as simple values, completely stripping custom getters, setters, `writable: false`, `enumerable: false`, and `configurable: false` flags. True property preservation requires `Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptors(obj)` paired with `Object.defineProperties()`.
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: Tests understanding of Property Descriptors vs simple property assignment.

interviewCrossQuestions.question: How do you clone Symbol-keyed properties?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: Standard `Object.keys()` only returns string keys. `Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptors()` and `Reflect.ownKeys()` capture both string keys AND symbol keys, ensuring complete own property preservation.
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: Checks awareness of ES6 Symbol property enumeration.

realWorldUseCases.scenario: Cloning Objects with Getters and Setters
realWorldUseCases.description: Cloning reactive objects (e.g. Vue reactive proxies or MobX observables) without prematurely executing or flattening getter properties.
Cloning and sealing security configurations where non-writable, non-configurable security flags must remain intact.

howToExplain.opening: A faithful shallow clone copies not just values, but the complete property descriptors (getters, setters, writability, configurability, and symbols) using Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptors.
keyPoints: Spread {...obj} and Object.assign only copy values and strip descriptors.
Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptors captures value, writable, get, set, enumerable, and configurable.
Reflect.ownKeys captures both string and symbol property keys.
Object.defineProperties applies descriptors accurately without triggering getter invocations.
howToExplain.closingImpression: Copying descriptors rather than invoking getters is essential when dealing with reactive state containers and classes.
analogies: Photocopying a document (Object.assign) vs duplicating the digital template file with all security permissions and formulas intact (defineProperties).

commonMistakes.mistake: Assuming spread {...obj} clones getters as getters.
commonMistakes.why: Spread evaluates the getter immediately and assigns the returned value as a static, plain property.
commonMistakes.correct: Use Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptors to copy the getter function itself.

followUpDeepDive.question: What is the difference between a Data Descriptor and an Accessor Descriptor?
followUpDeepDive.answer: A Data Descriptor contains `value` and `writable`. An Accessor Descriptor contains `get` and `set`. A property descriptor can NEVER contain both `value`/`writable` and `get`/`set` simultaneously; doing so throws TypeError.
